# Code of conduct

This is a small project about making game art. The rules are short because the standard is simple:
behave the way you would want a stranger to behave towards you.

This is deliberately not the Contributor Covenant. It says the same things in this repository's own
words, and it is the same standard [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) already sets for everything committed
here — everything in this repository is world-readable and permanent, and it is written as though a
stranger will read it tomorrow, because they can.

## What is expected

- **Stay on the work.** Discuss the code, the prompt text, the artwork and the defect. Not the
  person who wrote it.
- **Assume the other person is trying.** A confusing issue report, a wrong patch or an
  awkwardly-worded question is somebody making an effort in a second language, on a bad day, or with
  less context than you have.
- **Be direct and be kind.** Saying plainly that an approach is wrong is not rudeness. Saying it
  with contempt is.
- **Keep it professional and neutral.** No profanity, no jokes at anyone's expense, and no venting
  in code, comments, issues or commit messages.
- **Respect the maintainer's decision.** A change can be correct and still not be wanted. "No" is an
  answer, and repeating the request louder is not an appeal.

## What is not acceptable

Harassment of any kind. Insults, and remarks aimed at who somebody is rather than at what they
wrote. Sexual language or imagery, and unwelcome attention of any sort. Publishing anybody's private
information without their permission. Sustained disruption of a discussion. Anything else a
reasonable person would recognise as unprofessional.

This applies wherever the project is: issues, pull requests, discussions, commit messages, and
anywhere someone is representing the project in public.

## Reporting

Report a problem privately to the maintainer, [@BootBlock](https://github.com/BootBlock), through
GitHub. If a report is easier to make some other way, say so in a
[discussion](https://github.com/BootBlock/SpriteGubbins/discussions) without naming anyone and a
route will be arranged.

Every report is read and answered. Nothing about a report is shared beyond what is needed to act on
it.

## What happens then

The maintainer decides, and there is no committee to appeal to — this is a one-person project and
pretending otherwise would be a fiction. Depending on what happened, the response is a private word,
an edit or removal of the content, or a block from the repository. Behaviour that continues after a
warning gets the last of those.
